title: Cloud Security Finding Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `sourcetype IN ("aws:securityhub:finding", "azure:defender:alert", "gcp:scc:finding")` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.6.3 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `sourcetype IN ("aws:securityhub:finding", "azure:defender:alert", "gcp:scc:finding")`. Confirm UC-4.6.3 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center — forwarded via HEC or add-on; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center — forwarded via HEC or add-on
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" sourcetype IN ("aws:securityhub:finding", "azure:defender:alert", "gcp:scc:finding")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.3_cloud_security_finding_t_3"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.6.3 — Cloud Security Finding Trending: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for search criteria `sourcetype IN ("aws:securityhub:finding", "azure:defender:alert", "gcp:scc:finding")` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Cloud Security Finding Trending' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.6.3 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Map your findings feed so each event represents a finding state change or daily snapshot with Severity and status. For snapshot models, compare consecutive days to derive new and resolved counts via summary search. Align severities (Critical/High/Medium) across clouds for a combined view or use separate panels per provider. Refresh suppression lookups so trends reflect true risk.
visualization: Stacked column chart (new vs resolved per day), line chart (open critical count trend), area chart (cumulative open findings).
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center — forwarded via HEC or add-on with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Map your findings feed so each event represents a finding state change or daily snapshot with Severity and status. For snapshot models, compare consecutive days to derive new and resolved counts via summary search. Align severities (Critical/High/Medium) across clouds for a combined view or use separate panels per provider. Refresh suppression lookups so trends reflect true risk.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" sourcetype IN ("aws:securityhub:finding", "azure:defender:alert", "gcp:scc:finding")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.3_cloud_security_finding_t_3"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=cloud` to detect cloud security finding trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_3_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Stacked column chart (new vs resolved per day), line chart (open critical count trend), area chart (cumulative open findings)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center — forwarded via HEC or add-on and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud security finding trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
